title: Playlist and Semester
premise: Seventeen-year-old Quentin Coldharbour keeps her family afloat while her mother works night shifts, hiding her home life behind perfect grades and a locked-down reputation. Inside her late grandmother's recipe box she finds coded instructions pointing to an underground academic decathlon — the 'championship that matters' — whose winner receives a scholarship and access to records about her grandmother's erased past. To compete, Quentin must join the school's failing quiz team, risking exposure of her secret responsibilities, and untangle whether her loyal teammates are being used by a coach who knows more than he says. In the final round, Quentin chooses truth over the safe lie that would guarantee victory, exposing the coach's fraud, winning the scholarship on merit, and finally letting her siblings and friends see who she really is.
about_author: Sable Eriksen grew up in a coastal mill town where library cards were passports and every kitchen drawer hid somebody's secrets. A former debate coach and midnight-shift barista, she writes stories about kids who hold families together with duct tape and stubbornness.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. A Tuesday in the Coldharbour household: packing lunches for siblings Marisol and Dev, covering for Mom's double shift, acing a chem quiz without raising her hand. Establishes her invisibility rules. Emotional beat: quiet pride curdling into loneliness when no one at school knows her name.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Sorting Grandma Ruth's belongings after the funeral, Quentin finds a card labeled 'Biscuits' containing coordinates, dates, and a cipher key instead of ingredients. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into curiosity — Grandma was hiding something, and chose Quentin to find it.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. At school, guidance counselor Ms. Okafor flags Quentin's 'unclaimed potential' and mentions the quiz team's open roster. Quentin deflects. Meanwhile Dev gets in trouble for fighting a kid who mocked their mom. Emotional beat: the cost of staying invisible is starting to show on the people she loves.

chapters.title: Cipher Kitchen
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Late night decoding: the recipe cards map to a decades-old competition called the Meridian Trials, hosted by the district's founding families, with a scholarship prize. The last card reads 'For the granddaughter who counts everything.' Emotional beat: wonder — someone saw her, all along.

chapters.title: Tryouts and Tuna Casserole
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Quentin auditions for the quiz team as cover to access Meridian archives in the school basement, expecting to fail quietly. She doesn't. Team captain Priya Nair is suspicious; slacker-genius Theo Wren is delighted. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging, like a shoe that almost fits.

chapters.title: The Coach Who Waits
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Coach Aldous Vane, who 'coincidentally' knew Grandma Ruth, takes special interest in Quentin, feeding her practice materials and probing what she knows about the Trials. Emotional beat: flattery with a hook in it — Quentin can't tell if she's recruited or baited.

chapters.title: Marisol Finds Out
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Marisol discovers the recipe box and assumes Quentin is planning to leave for college and abandon them; a fight erupts over dishes, money, and silence. Emotional beat: guilt — Quentin realizes secrecy has read as betrayal at home.

chapters.title: Sectionals
chapters.summary: POV Priya. First competition: the ragtag team overperforms thanks to Quentin's pattern-recognition. Vane pushes them hard toward regionals, hinting the Meridian Trials ride on it. Emotional beat: Priya's hunger to matter, mirroring Quentin's need to hide — two opposite survival strategies.

chapters.title: What Grandma Buried
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Following a cipher clue to the county archive, Quentin learns Ruth competed in the 1978 Trials and was disqualified for exposing the judges' rigged scoring — then erased from records. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed; truth-telling runs in the family.

chapters.title: Theo's Theory
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo notices Quentin's odd research and, instead of blackmailing her, offers help — his own scholarship depends on the Trials too. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance; Theo's humor masking real desperation.

chapters.title: Mom Comes Home Early
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Mom loses a shift and catches Quentin mid-decode; instead of anger, she reveals she always suspected Ruth left something 'for the smart one.' Emotional beat: fragile relief — but Mom warns that the founding families don't forgive, foreshadowing danger.

chapters.title: Regionals, Rigged
chapters.summary: POV Priya. At regionals, the team faces a rival school coached by a Meridian insider; a mis-scored round nearly eliminates them until Quentin catches the error publicly. They advance — and make an enemy. Emotional beat: vindication laced with dread.

chapters.title: Invitation Card
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. An embossed invitation arrives: the team qualifies for the Meridian Trials proper, held at the Harrow estate. Vane's coaching intensifies and grows controlling — he demands Quentin hand over 'Ruth's materials.' Emotional beat: the trap closing gently, politely.

chapters.title: Loyalty Test
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Vane offers Theo a private scholarship endorsement if he reports on Quentin's off-book research. Theo stalls, torn between his own future and the team. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. survival made explicit; Theo chooses silence, for now.

chapters.title: The Harrow Estate
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Preview tour of the estate: Quentin sneaks into the library and finds Ruth's name scratched from a founders' plaque, plus evidence Vane was the student judge who cast the deciding vote against her in 1978. Emotional beat: cold shock — her mentor is her grandmother's betrayer.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Vane discovers her snooping and gives an ultimatum: bring him the recipe box or the whole team is disqualified and Theo's endorsement dies. Quentin hides the box with Marisol. Emotional beat: fear weaponized against everyone she loves.

chapters.title: All Hands
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Quentin finally tells the team everything — the cipher, the Trials' history, Vane's ultimatum. Instead of fracturing, they plan together, using each member's strength. Emotional beat: the belonging she avoided becomes her armor.

chapters.title: Dev's Distraction
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The younger siblings insist on helping; Dev's knack for codes cracks the final recipe card, which contains proof of the 1978 rigging hidden in plain notation. Emotional beat: family as a team of its own — the two championships converge.

chapters.title: Trials Day
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. The Meridian Trials begin at the estate: oral rounds before the founding families, Vane watching, the forged score sheets in Quentin's bag. She competes brilliantly while waiting for the moment. Emotional beat: controlled fury; invisibility burned away under chandelier light.

chapters.title: The Question That Isn't on the Card
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Climax. In the final round, judges offer Quentin the win if she discredits Ruth's 'disgrace.' Instead she presents the decoded proof of the 1978 rigging and Vane's role, forfeiting the safe path. Chaos; the families convene; Theo and Priya back her testimony. Emotional beat: truth chosen at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Scored Fairly
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Fallout: Vane resigns under investigation; the board, cornered by publicity, reinstates Ruth's record and awards Quentin the scholarship on verified merit. The team places second — and celebrates like champions. Emotional beat: justice imperfect but real; loyalty rewarded without lies.

chapters.title: Playlist for the Ride Home
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Epilogue: the siblings cram into Mom's car, recipe box between them, Quentin's acceptance letter on the seat. She makes a playlist — one song per person who saw her this year. Emotional beat: resolution — invisible no longer, and no longer alone.
